Definition: a Libyan or inhabitant of interior Africa (only in plural)
BiblicalUsage: The Libyans were a people of North Africa who appear in Scripture as soldiers and allies in the armies of other nations. They marched with Shishak against Jerusalem, and Asa remembered them as part of the huge host God delivered into his hand when he relied on the LORD. Prophets name them again among the nations drawn into the wars of the last days and among the helpers of fallen Nineveh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Libyans remind us that no nation's strength stands on its own, and armies without number are nothing against the LORD. I hold that God rules over every people, whether they serve Him or march against His people, and history bends to His purposes.
